title: Record Gold Prices Are Changing What Diwali Shoppers Buy, Not Whether They Buy
excerpt: Toronto shoppers are choosing smaller pieces and spending more cautiously, while buyers in India shift to lightweight jewellery, coins and old-gold exchanges as prices stay near record highs.
body:
• Toronto-area Diwali shoppers are still buying gold, but CityNews reports they are choosing smaller jewellery items and spending more cautiously as prices stay near record levels.
  • Gold has risen roughly 55 per cent this year in Canadian reporting to top US$4,000 an ounce, and Canadian jewellers say a typical buyer may pay 25 to 40 per cent more depending on gold content.
  • The shift is global: the World Gold Council says Indian festive buyers are moving to lightweight jewellery, with old-gold exchanges accounting for more than 50 per cent of sales at some retailers.
  • Reader takeaway: if you are buying for Diwali, compare lighter and lower-carat pieces, coins and exchange value for old gold before paying heavy-piece prices.

Diwali gold buying has not stopped in Toronto. It has changed shape. CityNews Toronto reports shoppers ahead of the festival are buying smaller jewellery items and making more cautious spending decisions as gold prices rise, rather than walking away from a purchase that carries cultural and family weight at Diwali.

That pattern matches what jewellers across Canada and India describe this season: demand holds, weight falls. Buyers trade down to lighter pieces, lower carats, coins and bars, or bring old gold in to exchange, so the total spend stays closer to budget even as the per-gram price climbs.

Canada: hollow pieces, silver and 10-karat gold

Gold soared roughly 55 per cent year-to-date to top the US$4,000 per ounce mark, and hit US$4,300 in October, according to The Canadian Press reporting carried by Barchart. Colin Nash, president of the Canadian Jewellery Group, said consumers are still spending, but by lesser amounts. "I think that we're still going to get the traffic, it's just a question of how much and what are they going to be buying," he said.

James Poag, co-owner of James O. Poag Jewellers, said the product mix is changing: more lab-grown diamonds and larger hollow pieces instead of heavier cast pieces, more repairs, and more customers trading in older jewellery to repurpose into a new design. He estimated an average consumer might pay about 25 to 40 per cent more, depending on the gold content of the item. Larger brands are adjusting too: Mejuri introduced 10-karat solid gold products to offer a lower price point, alongside 14-karat gold, vermeil and sterling silver.

India: lightweight jewellery and old-gold exchange

The same trade-down is visible in the world's largest Diwali gold market. The World Gold Council said manufacturers are reporting healthy order flows and improving store footfall in the festive and wedding season, but buyers are choosing lightweight jewellery and old-gold exchanges to manage costs, according to Outlook Money.

India Bullion and Jewellers Association prices stood at Rs 14,315 per gram for 24-carat gold on October 22, 2026. That is down nearly 20 per cent from the record Rs 17,885 per gram on January 30, 2026, but still high enough to limit how much gold a household can buy. Old-gold exchange transactions rose more than 10 per cent year-on-year and accounted for over 50 per cent of sales at some retailers, the WGC said.

Listed Indian jewellers still grew sales by value. Revenues rose 20 to 30 per cent year-on-year in the July-September quarter, Senco Gold reported 29 per cent retail revenue growth with a focus on lightweight and 9-carat collections, and PC Jeweller reported a 28 per cent rise in consolidated sales. India's gold imports, meanwhile, fell to $1.8 billion in September, the lowest since March 2024, at roughly 20 tonnes, partly because recycled gold from exchanges supplied more of the market.

What this means for Diwali buyers

For diaspora families in Toronto and other North American cities, the practical choices mirror India's: a lighter necklace or smaller earrings instead of a heavy set, a coin or small bar when the purchase is mainly investment, and an exchange valuation on old gold before buying new. Jewellers in Canada also point price-sensitive buyers to sterling silver, vermeil and lab-grown diamonds.

The risk in waiting is timing. Canadian jewellers told The Canadian Press they do not expect a significant downward trend in gold prices, even after October's peak. Buyers who need a piece for Diwali itself have less room to wait than buyers who can stagger purchases over the wedding season.

What happens next

Attention turns to Dhanteras and Diwali sales volumes, and then to results from large chains such as Titan Company on November 5 and Kalyan Jewellers on November 10 in India. Those numbers will show whether higher value sales offset lower volumes, or whether record prices finally cut into festive demand.
